system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime

- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's preamble.** The statements that these terms are "market", were "settled at principal level" and are "FINAL and not intended to be re-opened" are the Seller's assertions, not facts in our record. Nothing in the Buyer's instructions confirms principal-level agreement. Treat the whole package as an opening position and mark up accordingly. Also note the Disclosure Letter is internally candid in ways the Seller Update is not (e.g. Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, bonuses in funds flow) – the Update repeatedly understates what the Letter admits.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** Cap at or near 100% of price for general warranties, or at minimum 50%; separate uncapped/price-capped regimes for fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities (see 004, 011, 016).
- **Recommendation:** Reject 20%; counter at 100% of price (fallback 50%) and ring-fence fundamental/tax/indemnities outside it.
- **Reason:** With ~AUD 7m+ of identified exposure (Riverlark, Bluefen revenue at risk, bonuses, Ironquay, incident, renewals), a 4.8m cap could be exhausted by known issues alone.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket; excess-only (deductible) recovery.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis ≤ AUD 10,000; basket ≤ AUD 120,000 (0.5%); tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded); related claims aggregated; thresholds not applying to fundamental, tax or indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with 10k / 120k tipping, aggregation of related claims, and carve-outs.
- **Reason:** The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 110k each) show how a 25k/no-aggregation structure lets related claims be sliced below thresholds.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months; plus a catch-all that any limitation applies to *all* Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general warranties (covering at least one full audit cycle); 7 years for tax; statutory limitation for fundamental/title; indemnities until the underlying liability is time-barred. Strike the catch-all.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months general and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.
- **Reason:** The default clause silently drags tax, title and indemnity claims into the 18-month window.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances) capped at 100% of price, no de minimis/basket, 6–7 year limitation.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright; insist on a separate fundamental regime.
- **Reason:** A defect in title to 100% of the shares is a total-loss event; a 20% cap for it is commercially indefensible.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** None offered. Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Express carve-out from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and wilful default by the Seller or its officers.
- **Recommendation:** Insert a standard fraud carve-out as a non-negotiable.
- **Reason:** Limiting liability for fraud is contrary to public policy and absent in any genuinely "market" draft.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and all publicly searchable records; disclosure letter expressly admits nothing (cl 1.4).
- **Buyer wants:** Only matters "fairly disclosed" with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no deemed disclosure of public registers or the data room at large; specific disclosures mapped to specific warranties; data room index agreed and attached.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure; require fair-disclosure standard and warranty-specific disclosure.
- **Reason:** Blanket data-room disclosure combined with the knowledge qualifier (007) would neutralise the warranty package entirely.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- **Buyer wants:** Delete. At most, limit to actual knowledge of a short named list of deal-team individuals, excluding advisers and excluding constructive/"discoverable" knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Delete the clause; if a fallback is forced, actual knowledge of 2–3 named persons only.
- **Reason:** "Discoverable" knowledge converts every DD finding into a disclosure and is the Seller's second route to the same result as 006.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller Update:** "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent. **Disclosure Letter:** no final written consent and no evidence conditions in cl 11.3 are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** Unconditional written Bluefen consent (and evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied) as a true condition precedent, in a form approved by Buyer; Seller "best endeavours"; Buyer right to terminate or price-adjust (Bluefen ≈ 30% of FY26 revenue) if not obtained.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a hard CP with Buyer sign-off on form; add a specific revenue-loss indemnity if consent is conditional or late.
- **Reason:** Losing a ~AUD 3.6m/30% customer post-signing is the single largest value risk and "reasonable endeavours" plus self-certified satisfaction gives no protection.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion".
- **Buyer wants:** Full repayment at Completion from the purchase price via funds flow, executed deed of release and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion as a Completion deliverable; no post-Completion release.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; pay-off letter, discharge and PPSR release at Completion, deducted from price.
- **Reason:** "Debt-free/cash-free" is the baseline – inheriting a secured AUD 3.2m facility is a direct breach of the agreed price basis.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420k closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow; Letter admits they are absent and silent on super/payroll tax/on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses plus superannuation, payroll tax and on-costs (budget ~AUD 500k gross) treated as Transaction Expenses/Debt-like items and deducted from the price in the funds flow, or paid by Seller pre-Completion with evidence; specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise in funds flow with on-costs and deduct from price; add indemnity.
- **Reason:** These crystallise on Completion inside the Company – if not deducted, the Buyer funds them twice.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open per DD-010); "considered adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** Payment of SOW3 fees and executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as Completion deliverables; indemnity covering loss of or defect in title to all Project Materials (not just the fee), uncapped or capped at price, outside basket/time limits.
- **Recommendation:** Require pre-Completion payment + confirmatory assignment; widen the indemnity to title/use of the IP.
- **Reason:** Under cl 7.3 the Company does not own the SOW3 deliverables until paid – the exposure is the IP, not the AUD 180k invoice.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material"; Letter admits ~1,240 records sent to a wrong external address, scope/access/notifiability unknown.
- **Buyer wants:** Completed investigation report pre-signing; determination (with legal advice) on OAIC/NDB notification; specific indemnity for all costs, fines, claims and customer losses arising from the incident, outside cap/basket/time limits; warranty that no other incidents exist; possible escrow/retention.
- **Recommendation:** Require investigation close-out before signing and a specific uncapped (or price-capped) indemnity; do not accept the "not material" characterisation.
- **Reason:** An unresolved notifiable data breach in a SaaS business carries regulatory, contractual (Bluefen/Mossvale) and reputational exposure the Seller cannot cap by assertion.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k (AUD 330k aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs"; Letter admits nothing on terminability, accrual or necessity.
- **Buyer wants:** Confirmation whether renewals are committed, terminable or already accrued; if committed and not in forecasts, treat as debt-like/working-capital adjustment; aggregation clause so they are one claim for threshold purposes.
- **Recommendation:** Diligence the three contracts together; price-adjust if committed and unbudgeted; ensure related-claims aggregation (see 002).
- **Reason:** Splitting one AUD 330k commitment into three AUD 110k items looks designed to test the de minimis/basket structure.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Single regime – all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"; one cap, one time bar, one threshold.
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes for (i) general warranties, (ii) fundamental/title, (iii) tax, (iv) specific indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, incident, bonuses, Bluefen), (v) fraud; each with its own cap, thresholds (or none) and limitation period; leakage/debt-free adjustments outside all limitations.
- **Recommendation:** Restructure Schedule/cl 12 into separate categories; reject "all Claims" language in 9.3/12.8/20.5.
- **Reason:** A single regime lets the known issues consume the cap and time-bars the long-tail risks (tax, title) first.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced solely by the share register at DD-012; Letter notes Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent ASIC search, review of register against constitution and share certificates, PPSR search for share security (Riverlark), confirmation no options/convertibles/pre-emptive rights; full title and no-encumbrance warranties in the fundamental category.
- **Recommendation:** Run independent title verification now (ASIC + PPSR) and do not rely on DD-012.
- **Reason:** A register is the Company's own record and may not reflect an unregistered security or Riverlark charge over the shares.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 25k/250k, 18 months).
- **Buyer wants:** Tax: full tax indemnity for pre-Completion periods, 7-year limitation, capped at price, no thresholds; GST/stamp duty allocation; tax covenant mechanics. IP: ownership and non-infringement warranties, confirmatory assignments from all contractors (including Ironquay), open-source compliance warranty; IP warranties in or near the fundamental category given it is a SaaS business.
- **Recommendation:** Reject folding tax/IP into the general regime; insert a standalone tax indemnity and elevated IP warranties.
- **Reason:** Tax exposures surface on ATO audit cycles well beyond 18 months, and IP is the core asset being bought.

---

### Overall recommendation
Respond with a full mark-up rejecting the "FINAL" characterisation, prioritising: (1) Riverlark discharge and bonuses in the funds flow (price basis), (2) Bluefen consent as a hard CP, (3) category separation with fraud carve-out and fundamental/tax regimes, (4) deletion of general disclosure and the knowledge qualifier, (5) specific indemnities for Ironquay, incident and bonuses. Consider a retention/escrow of ~AUD 2–3m pending Bluefen consent and incident close-out.
=== END ADVICE ===
